component.name: LeafMD
component.summary: Read and edit markdown your way

description.p: LeafMD is a markdown viewer and editor that keeps things simple. Read a document cleanly formatted, work directly in the raw text, or see both side by side and watch your changes appear as you type.

Rather than trying to do everything, LeafMD focuses on doing the essentials well. There are no plugins to manage, panels to arrange or settings to tune, just a fast, dependable app that feels obvious from the moment you open it.

ul.li: Switch between formatted, raw and split views with one click or Ctrl+1, 2 and 3
A formatted-only view for pure, distraction-free reading
Tabs keep several documents in one window, and reopen when you start LeafMD again
Edit the raw text with the formatted view updating as you type
A formatting bar adds bold, links, lists, headings, tables and more for you
Lists continue themselves when you press Enter, and pasting a web address over text makes a link
A built-in markdown cheatsheet shows the common syntax at a glance
Find and replace, in the raw text or the formatted document
A banner tells you when another app changes your file, and nothing is overwritten without asking
In split view, both sides scroll together
Supports tables, task lists, footnotes and other GitHub-style markdown
Open files from a terminal with an optional short leafmd command
Follows your system's light or dark style

screenshot.caption: Edit markdown with the formatting bar
Watch your changes appear side by side as you type

description.p: LeafMD now has tabs, so one window can hold everything you're working on.

ul.li: Any file you open gets its own tab, including from your file manager and from links. The tab bar appears once a window has two documents
Each tab keeps its own text, view, undo history, find bar and banner
Drag a tab to reorder it, move it to another window or pull it out into a new one
Starting LeafMD brings back the saved files from the window you closed last, in the same tabs
Keyboard changes: Ctrl+T starts a new document, Ctrl+N opens a new window, and Ctrl+W closes the tab rather than the window. Ctrl+Q closes the window with all its tabs
Right-clicking LeafMD's icon offers New Window
Ctrl+Z now works straight after clicking Replace All
If you set up the short leafmd command before this version, run the setup again to use options like --new-window from any folder. See leafmd.app for the steps

description.p: LeafMD is now easier to use from a terminal.

ul.li: Starting LeafMD from a terminal now gives the terminal back straight away, and LeafMD stays open if you close the terminal
A one-time setup adds a short leafmd command, so leafmd notes.md opens a file. Help links to the steps
The new --foreground option keeps LeafMD attached to the terminal, to show its messages when something goes wrong

description.p: LeafMD now fits windows as small as 360 by 300 pixels. In a narrow window, the New, Save and Find buttons and the view buttons move to a bar along the bottom, and the find bar wraps onto extra rows.

ul.li: A banner now tells you when another app changes or deletes your open file, so you can reload it or keep what you have. Save also asks before replacing a version you haven't seen
A new button next to Open starts a new document with one click
Save is now a labelled button, just left of the view switcher
Open and its recent files arrow now look like one raised button
LeafMD now draws its own icons for the window's buttons, Find, the main menu and more, so they look the same on every Linux distribution
New Close Document item in the main menu takes you back to the "No Document Open" page, and LeafMD starts there next time too
Clear Recent Files now also forgets your last file, and is available even when the only recent file is the one you have open
Icons now look the same on every Linux distribution, including a floppy disk for Save
The Keyboard Shortcuts window is simpler, with no search box, and now also lists Ctrl+Q
Saving a file now moves it to the top of your recent files

description.p: LeafMD's page in your app store now shows screenshots of the formatted, raw and split views. Nothing else changes.
The first release of LeafMD, a simple markdown viewer and editor.

ul.li: Read a document formatted, edit the raw text, or see both side by side as you type
A formatting bar and a built-in cheatsheet for bold, links, lists, headings, tables and more
Lists continue when you press Enter, and pasting a web address over text makes a link
Find and replace, in the raw text or the formatted document
Install from leafmd.app, and get updates through your app store
